Class RefineOperator

java.lang.Object
ca.mcscert.jpipe.operators.CompositionOperator
ca.mcscert.jpipe.operators.builtin.RefineOperator
public final class RefineOperator extends CompositionOperator
Built-in refine composition operator.

Syntax: 

justification result is refine(base, refinement) {
    hook: "elementId"
}

Semantics: the hook element (identified by its id in the first source model) and the conclusion of the second source (refinement) are merged into a single SubConclusion named "hook". All other elements are kept with their source model name as id prefix (e.g. base:c, refinement:s).

The hook id is resolved through the unit alias map, so it can refer to an element that was renamed by a prior composition step (e.g. unification after assemble).

    • idArguments

      protected Map<String, Composition.Scope> idArguments()
      Description copied from class: CompositionOperator
      Declares which argument keys of this operator hold element ids, and where those ids name an element: in a source, as that source names it, such as refine's hook, or in the result. A call read from a file loaded under a namespace renames the qualified ids they hold, as it renames its source models, and so does the JPIPE export of the result. unifyExclude is declared by the framework (see CompositionOperator.idArgumentScopes()). Default: none.
      Overrides:

    • resultKind

      protected ModelKind resultKind(List<JustificationModel> sources, Map<String,String> arguments, List<Command> elements)
      A template when the result keeps an abstract support, one the hook did not replace; a justification otherwise. Decided from the elements the composition built, so it cannot disagree with the hook it refined: a refine could only produce a justification, so refining a template that keeps a @support failed (#181).
      Specified by:
      resultKind in class CompositionOperator
      Parameters:
      sources - the source models being composed, so that the kind can follow theirs.
      elements - the commands creating the result's elements, in Phase 1.
